surface_mechanism_description: The transamination reaction between chemisorbed TDMA T on the substrate and NH3 forms TiN, with subsequent purging steps removing reaction products. Plasma treatment aids in reducing carbon impurities by removing dimethylamino species.
evidence: When NH3 was pulsed into the reactor, TiN was formed via the well-known transamination reaction with chemisorbed TDMA T on the substrate and purged with Ar–H2 for 15 s. One of the reasons for the decrease [in carbon impurities] is thought to be that Ar–NH3–H2 radicals help to remove the dimethylamino species remaining in the TiN film.
